primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Chronic Q fever endocarditis due to Coxiella burnetii
mechanism: Coxiella burnetii is a Gram-negative obligate intracellular bacterium with a distinctive ability to replicate in an acidified phagolysosome-like Coxiella-containing vacuole. Humans typically acquire infection by inhaling contaminated aerosols from infected livestock. Chronic infection can produce culture-negative endocarditis, especially in patients with preexisting valvular or vascular abnormalities; high phase I IgG titers support chronic Q fever.
vignette: A 49-year-old man with a previously diagnosed bicuspid aortic valve has 3 months of fatigue, intermittent fever, and weight loss. He works on a goat and sheep farm and frequently assists with animal deliveries. A new regurgitant murmur is present. Multiple routine blood cultures remain sterile. Serologic testing shows a markedly elevated phase I IgG antibody titer to an intracellular bacterium.
lead: Which of the following intracellular adaptations is most characteristic of the causative organism?
correct: Replication within an acidified phagolysosome-like vacuole in host cells
distractors: Escape from the phagosome into the cytosol through a pore-forming hemolysin
Prevention of phagosome-lysosome fusion by arresting phagosomal maturation
Formation of membrane-bound microcolonies primarily within circulating neutrophils
Intracellular conversion to elementary bodies followed by reticulate-body replication in a nonacidic inclusion
distractor_notes: Phagosomal escape through listeriolysin O is characteristic of Listeria monocytogenes, not Coxiella burnetii.
Inhibition of phagolysosomal fusion is a classic survival strategy of Mycobacterium tuberculosis; Coxiella instead tolerates and exploits an acidic phagolysosome-like compartment.
Morulae within granulocytes are associated with Anaplasma phagocytophilum rather than Coxiella.
Elementary-body/reticulate-body cycling in an intracellular inclusion is characteristic of Chlamydia species.
key_expl: Livestock exposure, culture-negative endocarditis, underlying valvular disease, and high phase I IgG strongly indicate chronic Q fever due to Coxiella burnetii. Unlike many intracellular pathogens that avoid lysosomal fusion, Coxiella directs formation of a mature acidic phagolysosome-like vacuole and replicates within it. Routine hospital blood cultures generally do not detect the organism.
objective: Recognize chronic Q fever endocarditis and distinguish Coxiella burnetii by its unusual ability to replicate within an acidic phagolysosome-like intracellular compartment.
